title: Synapse capability descriptor
description: What a Synapse capability declares about itself. EXTRACTED from building resolvers, not designed in advance: every field here exists because a resolver could not be written without it. Fields 1-7 came from current_state; preconditions came from daily_series, which cannot answer usefully for a tenant with twelve days of history and so turned resolution into 'can this be satisfied FOR THIS TENANT, RIGHT NOW'. Two resolvers is still a small sample, so this schema stays narrow — cost/latency classes, caching, substitution rules, pagination shape and capability composition are ABSENT because two samples cannot justify them.

id.description: Stable capability name. snake_case; a consumer names this to ask for it.

version.description: SemVer. Matches the C6 pack contract's version discipline; the shape of an answer changes over time and a consumer must be able to pin it.

grain.description: The column names that together identify ONE row. Without a declared grain a consumer cannot join two capabilities or know what a row IS, and every analytics mistake downstream starts there.

tenancy.description: tenant_scoped = the scope's tenant is required and the read cannot widen. fleet = a deliberate cross-tenant read. No capability declares fleet today; the value exists so a future one must SAY so rather than acquire the ability by omitting a field.

freshness.description: last_write = the value as of whenever the row was last written; no date parameter is meaningful. as_of_date = stamped with the date it describes, so a series exists. The distinction is here because conflating them lets a consumer average a point-in-time reading against a time series with no layer objecting.

returns.description: The projection's field names — what the caller actually receives. Deliberately NOT canonical's full row: DIS write-side provenance (mapping_version_id, trace_id, ingest_metadata, dis_channel) is DIS's concern, and passing it through would invite the analytics plane to reason about ingestion.

produces_signals.description: Signal ids this capability PRODUCES. An EMPTY ARRAY is a first-class, verified state, not a placeholder: current_state reads canonical.store_sku_current_position, which HAS velocity_7day / stock_age_days / unit_cost_trend_30day, and produces none of them because nothing writes them. Reading a signal column does not make a capability a producer of that signal — which is exactly why signals are a separate contract.

preconditions.description: Conditions that must hold FOR A GIVEN TENANT before this capability can be resolved. Declared here rather than on the resolver because a consumer must be able to learn the requirement WITHOUT calling: it is the only way an operator console can tell 'no such capability' apart from 'this capability exists and this tenant is 48 days short of it'. An EMPTY ARRAY is a claim, not a placeholder — current_state reads the hot table, where no quantity of history makes an answer usable or unusable, so there is genuinely nothing to require. The MEASUREMENT is not described here: it names a canonical table and so belongs to synapse.resolvers (D6).

items.description: ONE KIND EXISTS. A generic (name, operator, value) triple invented from one sample would be a guess, so `kind` is a const rather than an enum and `days` is required outright: adding a second kind means editing this schema into a oneOf, which is a visible change rather than a new string flowing through an open shape.

days.description: Minimum number of DISTINCT dates carrying data in scope — coverage, not calendar span. A tenant onboarded 90 days ago that sold on 12 of them has coverage 12. Minimum 1: a threshold of 0 is not a precondition, it is a declaration that there is none, and that is what the empty array says.
